title: GPU memory splay and KeyCache coherence restoration (customer escalations across Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported sudden GPU OOM spikes accompanied by long-tail latency and session failures. Root cause analysis indicates a KeyCache coherence anomaly that causes unbounded slab scattering (we're calling it 'memory splay') under heterogeneous request distributions; the scatter prevents compaction heuristics from reclaiming GPU arenas and leads to OOM waves. This ticket coordinates the emergency fix, validation, rollback plan, and customer communications for a surgical runtime patch and a medium-term refactor.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Triage: Incident reported by two Hosted customers (high-traffic chat) and one Dedicated customer during nightly batch. Alerts: GPU memory saturation + eviction thrashing. Assigned to Diego. Initial mitigation: increased eviction aggressiveness and per-session token cap for affected tenants. Noted Private deployment had different allocator behavior but similar outcome.

2026-03-10 - Investigation: Heap snapshots from a Dedicated node show thousands of tiny KeyCache handles pinned to remote slabs; compactor was skipping ranges due to stale coherence markers. Hypothesis: concurrent insert path races set 'active' markers without clearing tombstones under high prefix-sharing workloads (long conversations + multi-turn prompts).

2026-03-11 - Mitigation deployed (hosted hotfix): small runtime flag 'kc_soft_rebuild=true' enabled which triggers opportunistic KeyCache soft-rebuilds during low-util windows and forces a full arena sweep on owner rotation. Immediate effect: memory pressure subsided on 2/3 impacted clusters. Continued monitoring.

2026-03-11 - Reproduction: Created synthetic workload that reproduces memory splay using multi-tenant prefix storm generator (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/kc-repro). Repro steps and benchmark harness added to reproducer. Dedicated reproduction validated on rtx-pool-2; Private customer reproduced in staging with their model fork.

2026-03-12 - Patch PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4021. Patch does three things: 1) stronger ordering on KeyCache insert/remove (compare-and-wait backoff), 2) fast-path tombstone reclamation in the compactor, 3) slab realignment routine to coalesce fragmented arenas without full stop-the-world GC. Initial unit tests added and fuzz harness extended.

2026-03-12 - QA: Patch applied to a Dedicated canary cluster (canary-oom-3). Ran 24h soak with mixed chat/embedding workload (~60% chat). Observed stable memory curve, no OOM. Latency improved by ~8% for 99p token times. Identified a minor regression: slightly higher p50 CPU due to additional synchronization; scheduled micro-optimizations.

2026-03-13 - Code review: Two approvals from runtime team and one from infra-systems. Security reviewed no secrets impact. PR size small but touches critical allocator paths; recommend staged rollout with circuit breaker and telemetry flags.

2026-03-13 - Communications: Drafted customer advisory for affected tenants (ID: CA-2026-03-KC). Notifying Support and CSMs; will include workarounds (session token cap and nightly soft-rebuild flag) and ETA for patch rollout once canary passes full regression suite.

2026-03-13 - Next steps: finish micro-optimizations on fast-path, broaden canary to Hosted region-us-west-2 (mixed fleet), validate Private installer packaging, schedule maintenance window for Dedicated customers requiring forced rebuilds. Postmortem and long-term refactor ticket to follow.

Operational notes: Keep 'kc_soft_rebuild' feature flagged and monitor metric 'kc_coherence_errors' and 'gpu_arena_compaction_rate'. Add alert: if compaction_rate < 0.5x baseline and gpu_free_memory drops > 20% in 5m, auto-trigger partial session drain and escalate to on-call.

Rollback plan: When rollout begins, patch is feature-flagged. If critical regressions occur, flip 'kc_patch_enable=false' and enable aggressive evict throttle (runtime flag 'evict_throttle=aggressive'). Ensure we have snapshot and repro harness archived for forensic follow-up.
postmortem_plan: Once patch verifies in production (72h stable across canaries and two Hosted regions), publish full postmortem detailing root cause, timeline, code changes, test coverage improvements, and a follow-up refactor ticket to replace current KeyCache coherence markers with a linearizable epoch protocol. Also schedule a customer-facing RCA for the most impacted tenants.
